text:
Kyle Palmieri snapped a ten-game goal drought 20 seconds into Thursday's game in Winnipeg, and NHL.com's Stefen Rosner pointed out what our numbers say too: he'd been getting his chances. Palmieri has 4 goals on 6.2 expected this season and 8 points in 21 games, below the rate he managed last season in an injury-shortened 25 games.

Newsday has written about his struggle to produce, and the points are light. The process is better than that. At five on five the Islanders take 53% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly five points better than without him, and he's playing 16 to 17 minutes a night. His shooting is at 9.5%, the bottom of the 9.5% to 14% range we'd expect from him.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample of eight games last season, had him finishing a lot of passes across the slot, the kind that go in at four times the rate of a shooter's own play. The Long Island kid is 35 and in his sixth season with his hometown team. One goal doesn't end a slump, but the chances say more are coming.
headline: Palmieri finally gets one to go in
